ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Primary AML/CFT rules are in the French Monetary and Financial Code, Articles L561-1 to L561-50 and related regulatory provisions, implementing EU AML directives and applicable Financial Action Task Force standards. Beneficial-owner identification and filing rules principally arise under Articles L561-46 to L561-50 and Articles R561-1 to R561-3 and R561-55 to R561-63 of the Monetary and Financial Code, together with the French Commercial Code provisions governing the national register of enterprises. The beneficial-owner declaration is filed through the INPI single electronic formalities portal and maintained in the Registre National des Entreprises. Decree No. 2017-1094 of 12 June 2017 established the beneficial-owner declaration framework. Public access to beneficial-owner data is restricted following the Court of Justice of the European Union judgment of 22 November 2022 in Joined Cases C-37/20 and C-601/20; competent authorities and obliged entities retain statutory access.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before incorporation, banking and onboarding, screen all shareholders, directors, beneficial owners, authorized signatories, key intermediaries and material counterparties against United Nations Security Council lists, European Union financial sanctions, French national sanctions administered through competent French authorities, OFAC SDN and other relevant OFAC lists, and reputable commercial sanctions databases. Conduct PEP and close-associate screening using current and historical data, obtain source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence for PEPs and high-risk persons, apply enhanced due diligence and senior-management approval where required, document false-positive resolution, and perform continuing monitoring. French obliged entities must apply the risk-based AML/CFT framework under the Monetary and Financial Code and report suspicions to TRACFIN where legally required. OFAC screening is directly mandatory for US persons and US nexus transactions and is commercially relevant for USD, US-bank and US-platform exposure; it is not a universal substitute for French and EU sanctions compliance.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises, operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI): https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; resulting registration is recorded in the Registre National des Entreprises
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be included in the articles and filing in a form accepted under French company law. French is the official filing language; foreign words, acronyms and transliterations may generally be used if they are not misleading, unlawful, contrary to public policy or confusingly similar to an existing protected name. The suffix 'Société à responsabilité limitée' or 'SARL' must identify the legal form. Name clearance should cover the RNE, commercial-name and establishment-name records, INPI trademark databases, domain names and relevant EUIPO records. Registration does not itself confer trademark ownership or eliminate infringement risk.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, banque, credit institution, établissement de crédit, payment institution and equivalent regulated-finance terms without the required authorization or wording approval
Insurance, assurance, réassurance, mutual insurance and equivalent regulated-insurance terms without authorization
Investment company, portfolio management, financial market and equivalent regulated-activity terms without authorization
Public authority, ministry, national institution, European institution, diplomatic or governmental terms likely to create official affiliation or confusion
Lawyer, avocat, notary, notaire, accountant, expert-comptable and other regulated-profession designations unless used by an appropriately authorized entity
Medical, pharmaceutical, healthcare and other protected professional designations where the proposed activity or entity lacks the required authorization
Terms that are discriminatory, defamatory, unlawful, contrary to public order or misleading as to the company's activity, nationality, status or regulatory approval
Names confusingly similar to existing registered companies, trademarks, trade names or well-known brands, even where no automatic ministerial approval is required
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not generally provide a nationwide statutory company-name reservation mechanism with a fixed reservation period. Conduct clearance before signing the articles, secure the relevant domain names and, where brand protection is required, file an INPI or EUIPO trademark application. If the INPI single-window filing is rejected or suspended, obtain the electronic rejection notice and identified deficiency, correct the filing or upload supporting evidence within the stated deadline, and resubmit through the portal. For a formal administrative decision, request reconsideration from the issuing authority and use the applicable administrative or judicial appeal route, generally before the competent administrative court or commercial court depending on the nature of the dispute. A rejection based on trademark or company-name infringement may require a consent letter, amended name, coexistence agreement or separate court proceedings. No incorporation should proceed using a name that infringes a prior right.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A French SARL must have a registered office in France. A commercial domiciliation company may be used if it is properly authorized and the company has a written domiciliation agreement satisfying the French Commercial Code. A director may, subject to statutory conditions and duration limits, use a personal residence as the registered office. A bare postal box or address lacking legally valid premises access is insufficient. For computerized embroidery, ultrasonic seaming and plush-toy OEM activities, a virtual registered office may be acceptable for incorporation and administrative purposes, but it does not replace premises, equipment, staff, inventory controls, product-safety records, customs records or operational substance where those functions are actually performed in France. The company must comply with applicable EU and French toy-safety, product-safety, labeling, traceability, consumer-protection, VAT, customs and environmental obligations. No general sector incorporation license is assumed, but product compliance and importer or manufacturer obligations must be separately verified.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: No statutory inspection probability is published. For a low-risk standard plush-toy manufacturing and OEM profile using a compliant domiciliation provider, the estimated baseline risk of an unannounced physical address verification during the first 12 months is approximately 5% to 15%, subject to bank, customs, tax, AML, product-safety and labor-risk indicators. The risk increases materially if the address is shared excessively, the company has no documented operations, turnover is inconsistent with substance, beneficial ownership is opaque, customs declarations are anomalous, or the registered office is not operationally accessible.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.210-1 to L.210-10 and L.223-1 to L.223-43 governing the constitution and management of a Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL); implementing rules R.123-1 to R.123-20 concerning registration with the Registre du commerce et des sociétés (RCS).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du commerce et des sociétés (RCS), operated by the Greffe du tribunal de commerce in the jurisdiction of the registered office and accessed through the INPI Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts (articles of association) together with the electronic unique creation form and supporting evidence filed via the INPI Guichet Unique; registration produces the Kbis extract.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum SARL capital is imposed; the share capital is fixed freely in the articles. Cash contributions must be fully subscribed and at least one-fifth (20%) of each cash contribution must be paid up at formation, with the resulting funds deposited into a blocked bank account or held by a notary until the RCS registration is obtained. In-kind contributions must be fully paid and transferred on incorporation; unpaid cash balances may be called by the gérant within five years.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION ONE — SHARE SUBSCRIPTION: The shareholders irrevocably subscribe for the entire stated share capital of EUR 8,000, divided into 800 equal shares of EUR 10 each. Cash contributions are fully subscribed and placed in a blocked account with a French credit institution. RESOLUTION TWO — REGISTERED OFFICE: The registered office is established at [street address], Paris, France, and may be relocated by the gérant under legal notice procedures. RESOLUTION THREE — APPOINTMENT: [Name] is appointed as gérant for an indefinite term, with the fullest powers to operate the business, bind the company, and open bank accounts. RESOLUTION FOUR — REGISTRATION: The gérant is authorized to file all documents, publish notices, pay fees, and complete the RCS registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of the SARL Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Shareholders with French legal counsel; a notary must intervene if real property is contributed to the company.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the statuts containing the corporate name, registered office, corporate purpose covering computerized embroidery, ultrasonic seaming and OEM sale of plush mascots and stuffed toys, duration, share capital, contribution details, share distribution, management powers, and decision rules. Every shareholder must sign each page and the final execution page. If in-kind contributions exceed relevant thresholds, obtain a capital contribution auditor's report (commissaire aux apports).
required_dossiers: Signed Articles of Association (statuts)
Identity documents of all shareholders
Contribution valuation report or notarized inventory for in-kind contributions, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry identifies missing or defective statutory clauses, execute a corrective private-seal amendment and re-submit it within the same application window; no duplicate registration fee is charged for a cured application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the blocked capital account and deposit of cash contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A French credit institution or, alternatively, a notary holding the funds on escrow.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Provide the signed or draft statuts and manager identities to the selected bank and instruct the opening of a professional blocked account (compte bloqué) for the share capital. Transfer at least 20% of each cash contribution amount. The bank must issue a capital deposit certificate (attestation de dépôt des fonds) identifying the subscribers and the amount blocked; this certificate is required for the incorporation filing.
required_dossiers: Bank mandate form
Signed or draft Articles of Association
Identity documents of managers and shareholders
Deposit slip or transfer confirmation for the blocked amount
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the blockage certificate is defective, request a corrected certificate from the bank specifying the exact company name, all subscribers, the account-holder name and the deposit date; all data must match the statuts exactly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the legal formation announcement in a legal announcement newspaper
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'annonces légales (JAL) authorized to receive public notices in the department of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish the mandatory formation notice stating the legal form, company name, registered office, share capital, corporate object, names of the gérants and the RCS registry where the company will be filed. The newspaper issues a justificatif de parution with reservation number and publication date, which must be appended to the filing.
required_dossiers: Official text of the legal announcement
Receipt for JAL publication fees
Justificatif de parution issued by the newspaper
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the announcement is rejected for insufficient or ambiguous content, commission a corrected publication without restarting the underlying company-name reservation; a fresh justificatif de parution will be submitted to the Guichet Unique.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic submission of the creation dossier through the INPI Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI (Institut national de la propriété industrielle) portal at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create an account or log in, select creation of a Société à Responsabilité Limitée, complete the unified electronic form equivalent to the M0, upload the signed statuts, blocked-capital certificate, legal announcement certificate, beneficial-owner declaration, registered-office proof and manager identity documents. Pay the official registry fee online and submit; the platform issues an automatic acknowledgment of receipt and transmit the dossier to the competent RCS registry.
required_dossiers: Completed unified creation form
Signed Articles of Association
Bank capital blockage certificate
Justificatif de parution from the legal announcements journal
Declaration of beneficial owners
Proof of registered office (lease, utility bill, or owner consent)
Identity document of each gérant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the portal issues a completeness notice or draft refusal, reply within the prescribed 15-day period by uploading the missing documents or correcting the declaration through the Guichet Unique interface. A formal refusal may be cured by timely administrative contestation with INPI or by re-filing after correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS registration and issuance of the Kbis extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce having jurisdiction over the registered office, acting on the transfer from INPI.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After validation of the dossier, the registry verifies the legality of the statuts and supporting documents, registers the SARL, and issues the official Kbis extract. The blocked capital funds are released against presentation of the Kbis. The company thereby obtains its SIREN, SIRET and effective date for tax and social security registration.
required_dossiers: Automatically generated registration request
Proof of payment of registry fees
Any additional curative document requested by the registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry requests a supplementary document, provide it through the Guichet Unique messaging system. In the event of a refusal based on defective statutory clauses or prohibited corporate purposes, amend the articles and file a new application or challenge the decision before the President of the Commercial Court.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No sectoral manufacturing license is required for a plush toy OEM activity. Workplace safety and labor compliance are supervised by the DREETS (Direction régionale de l'économie, de l'emploi, du travail et des solidarités), and environmental matters by the DREAL where thresholds for classified installations are met.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — no industrial operation permit exists for low-risk computerized embroidery and ultrasonic seaming of custom plush dolls; product-level compliance under the EU Toy Safety Directive is required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: DREAL (Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from a full EIA for a non-ICPE plush toy assembly unit. If textile finishing, solvent use or waste thresholds raise the installation into the ICPE regime, a 'Déclaration' or 'Enregistrement' classification may apply.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: If ICPE thresholds are triggered, compliance with the French ICPE Title I regime, applicable ministerial orders on volatile organic compounds and wastewater discharge limits, and local municipal pre-treatment standards is required; otherwise EU Toy Safety Directive chemical limits and general sanitary standards apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For premises open to the public, fire safety approval by the commission de sécurité is required. For the production workshop, compliance with Code du travail requirements on fire exits, electrical installations, ventilation, first aid and building structural load shall be confirmed by the building owner or a licensed structural engineer.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) acting through the Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) for income tax and VAT; company registration with the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via the commercial court clerk (Greffe), now centralised through the Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a French SARL: (1) file articles of association and legal representative details with the RCS via the Guichet Unique; (2) obtain the Kbis extract, which issues the SIREN/SIRET identifiers; (3) the DGFiP automatically allocates the intra-EU VAT number (FR + two-digit key + SIREN) and registers the company for corporate income tax and VAT; (4) separate registration for French VAT is required if the entity is non-established and has no French permanent establishment, submitted to the SIE (or via the European Commission's one-stop-shop portal) using the French VAT registration form; (5) if importing/exporting physically, obtain an EORI number from the French Customs (Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: French law does not provide a US-style check-the-box election. A SARL is by default subject to corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS) at entity level. However, certain family SARLs or eligible small-scale SARLs (under CGI article 239 bis AA) may elect to be treated as pass-through partnerships (régime des sociétés de personnes), retaining shareholder-level income taxation. Additionally, a qualifying French group may elect for fiscal integration (intégration fiscale) under CGI articles 223 A et seq. Anti-hybrid mismatches are addressed through EU ATAD and French hybrid mismatch rules rather than elective mechanisms.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT / Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No universal turnover-eligibility threshold for mandatory VAT registration: any taxable person carrying out taxable supplies in France must be registered for VAT. For small traders, the 'franchise en base de TVA' exemption applies below €85,000 annual turnover for sale of goods (2024), but that is an exemption from charge rather than a registration threshold. Once turnover exceeds the threshold, registration and VAT collection are compulsory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing mandatory structured electronic invoicing in a phased timetable: from 1 September 2026 for large enterprises and from 1 September 2027 for SMEs and SARLs. All domestic B2B invoices must be transmitted through the national Portail Public de Facturation (PPF) or a certified private platform (PDP/OD) using standard formats (Factur-X, UBL, CII). The same phase requires real-time e-reporting of transaction data to the DGFiP, including cross-border supplies covered by the reverse charge. For typical OEM plush-mask/garment manufacturing, no digital stamping or continuous transaction metering is required; however, VAT returns must be filed electronically via the professional tax portal (e.g., Form CA3/CA12 using EDI mode).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export zero-rating applies under CGI article 262-I-1 where tangible goods (including plush mascots and stuffed animals) are physically transported outside the EU by the supplier, by a customer not established in France, or by a third party acting on their behalf; the goods must be delivered outside the EU and the export must be documented in accordance with the proof-of-export rules (CGI annex I articles 74-0 F to 74-0 J). Services directly tied to exported goods (such as custom embroidery or OEM manufacture for non-EU clients) are generally outside the scope of French VAT where the recipient is a foreign taxable person under B2B place-of-supply rules, often subject to reverse charge in the customer's jurisdiction.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration Administrative Unique / DAU with EXIT or ECS confirmation from French Customs)
Proof of physical exit from the EU (DELTA exit record / États de suivi de sortie)
Transport document (Bill of Lading, CMR, AWB or multimodal document showing exporter and EU exit point)
Commercial invoice and packing list (with clear reference to the export declaration)
Inward Remittance Certificate and bank statement demonstrating export proceeds received within the mandatory FX repatriation deadline
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If the export zero-rating is challenged or the required documentation is missing, the DGFiP may recharacterise the sale as taxable and assess French VAT at 20%, deny input VAT deduction, and apply late interest (0.20% monthly) plus negligence penalties of 40% or 80% for deliberate intent; fraudulent fictitious export transactions can incur criminal penalties up to €1.5 million fine and imprisonment. Any previously granted VAT export refund or credit may be clawed back as an undue repayment, and non-repatriation of export proceeds within the 180-day legal deadline triggers additional customs and exchange-control penalties under the French Monetary and Financial Code.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) acting as the national central bank, with foreign exchange regulatory and balance-of-payments functions exercised jointly with the Direction Générale du Trésor (DG Trésor) at the Ministry of Economy and Finance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is an IMF Article VIII member and the euro is fully convertible for current-account transactions and capital-account transactions within the EU. No prior exchange-control authorisation is required for equity injections, trade credits, profit distributions, or repatriation of branch proceeds, except for transactions with persons listed under EU financial sanctions or with entities domiciled in the non-cooperative jurisdictions named by the EU. Profit remittance from an SARL is subject only to corporate-law conditions, such as approval by the partners, absence of net-asset erosion, and demonstrated liquidity. The EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive eliminates French withholding tax when an EU parent holds at least 5% of the SARL's capital; for a non-EU treaty parent, treaty withholding tax rates generally range from 0% to 15%. Hurdles are therefore tax compliance and documentary formalities, not FX conversion.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France maintains no mandatory export-proceeds surrender rule and no statutory time-window for converting export receipts. Export proceeds may be freely retained in a foreign-currency account for the commercial credit period, and no conversion ratio or central-bank allocation is imposed. Reporting obligations remain: every flow between a resident and a non-resident must be declared to the Banque de France for balance-of-payments statistics through the reporting bank or directly; physical cash movements of €10,000 or more are separately declarable to customs.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for ancillary collection accounts, Low for primary treasury rails. Lawful French digital EMIs, such as Qonto and Shine, operate under ACPR licences and provide efficient remote onboarding, SEPA and SWIFT access in EUR, but as monoline payment institutions they lack credit lines, cannot issue documentary letters of credit, do not possess a universal correspondent banking passport for non-EU clearing, and are prohibited from paying interest or executing proprietary foreign-exchange forwards. Offshore EMIs not authorised in the EU are neither viable nor acceptable because they would trigger a negative AML determination from the appointed French correspondent bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is legally possible under the French Monetary Code and the ACPR digital-identity guidance when each signatory and UBO passes video identification with a substantial assurance level certificate or uses a certified electronic identity provider. Nevertheless, Tier-1 domestic banks generally require the SARL's gérant to appear physically at branch opening; remote identification is invoked only for passive non-resident UBOs. When all signatories are non-resident, a physical visit to a French branch, or a French-consular certified identity package, is ordinarily mandatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly formed SARL with a virtual registered address and no audited accounts seeking rapid high-volume import payments to Asia.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Company articles of association; Kbis extract less than three months old; proof of share capital payment; declaration of the beneficial owner; audited opening balance sheet; supplier and customer inventory; commercial contracts demonstrating the Chinese OEM supply chain; pro-forma invoices; transport documents; and a cash-flow model consistent with stated turnover.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business pattern of significant third-party marketplace payouts, interpreted by the bank as fund layering or concealment of commercial revenue.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified store-management reports from the online marketplaces; payment remittance extracts identifying each clearing; legally recognized e-invoice records identifying end consumers; revenue concentration and Herfindahl report; platform anti-fraud attestation; and an audit trail linking each payout to a corresponding customer order.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign UBO or signatory appearing on sanctions or PEP screening without a coherent explanation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions and PEP clearance from a reputable commercial database; passport and proof of residence; sworn statement of legitimate source of wealth and source of funds; corporate registry certificate of the owning company; share register evidencing ownership; and employment or directorship evidence linking the UBO to the operating business.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection sourced from a non-bank fintech, crypto gateway, or unknown third-party lender instead of the banked parent entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SWIFT MT103 from the parent's bank to the SARL capital escrow; corresponding bank statement of the parent in the same amount; share subscription act; shareholder resolution approving the capital increase; updated UBO declaration; and the mandatory balance-of-payments declaration submitted to the Banque de France.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing requires a SEPA Credit Transfer for EU-sourced capital or a SWIFT MT103 for non-EU inflows, with the beneficiary being the SARL's dedicated capital escrow account. The wire narrative must reference 'FR_SARL – souscription au capital – [date] [number of the share subscription act]' and include the standard BIC/IBAN destination. The associated payment purpose uses the EU CBPR message implementation guide code for foreign direct investment, enabling the receiving bank to populate the Banque de France balance-of-payments reporting line. The bank must also document the verified source of funds for any operation exceeding €15,000, in accordance with Article L561-15 of the French Monetary and Financial Code.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Import payments for raw materials and finished components to Chinese or Vietnamese suppliers clear via SWIFT MT103 or MT202, or through documentary credit instruments such as an irrevocable commercial L/C issued by the French bank (SWIFT MT700) with a sight or usance tenor. EUR payments to EU suppliers are cleared through SEPA. For settlement in renminbi, the SARL uses the offshore CNH corridor operated by London or Hong Kong clearing banks. Platform payouts to end consumers are accepted on marketplace payment rails and swept daily to the operational account. All outbound wires must reference the pro-forma invoice and French customs export or import declaration for audit traceability.
